beats.lead: Eat the frog is credited to Mark Twain
beats.text: The advice to do your worst task first is usually attributed to him.
beats.note: Brian Tracy's book Eat That Frog! opens with that credit.

beats.lead: Nobody has found Twain saying it
beats.text: Quote Investigator found no substantive evidence, and the first known Twain link is a 1988 newspaper column.

beats.name: Nicolas Chamfort
beats.role: French writer. His collected works credit a toad a day to M. de Lassay.

beats.text: The line was about swallowing a toad each morning so nothing in high society could disgust you later.
beats.note: It was a joke about society, not a task list.

beats.text: The frog is a toad, and the author is French.

beats.line: A famous tip, credited to the wrong century.
